sections.h2: Who collects property tax inside Cleveland city limits?
sections.html:
Two bills reach a Cleveland homeowner, one from the City of Cleveland and one from Bradley County. The Bradley County Assessor of Property values the parcel for both. Send the county bill to the Bradley County Trustee and the city bill to the city finance office.

  • City of Cleveland Finance: Municipal Building, 190 Church Street NE, open weekdays until 5 in the afternoon. Phone (423) 472-4551. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1519.
  • Bradley County Trustee: 1701 Keith Street NW, (423) 728-7247. Monday through Thursday the office keeps 8:30 to 4:30, and on Friday it stays open until 5.
  • Bradley County Assessor of Property: (423) 728-7126, for address changes, values and appeals.

The county also runs a toll-free automated payment line at (833) 591-7276.

City bills are mailed in the first week of October. Payment opens October 1 and stays penalty free until February 28 of the following year. Payment not received or postmarked by February 28 draws a 1.5 percent charge on March 1, and the same again each month after.

That charge builds to a cap of 18 percent, which takes twelve months. After that, unpaid taxes go to the Bradley County Clerk and Master. County tax is also due by the end of February.

sections.h2: What is the Cleveland and Bradley County tax rate?
sections.html:
The county's net rate for 2025 is .9922 on each $100 of assessed value. Two fire district surcharges exist, .2182 inside the fire fringe and .2408 outside it, but they apply only to county-only properties and not to a house inside Cleveland.

For the city rate, call the finance office at (423) 472-4551 and ask what is current. Homes are assessed at 25 percent of appraised value across Tennessee. Add the county rate and the city rate together, apply them to that assessed figure, and you have the picture a buyer will see.

Bradley County runs the state Tax Relief program through the Trustee's office and operates its own Tax Freeze for owners 65 and older. The City Clerk's office can also take state relief applications at the Municipal Building.

  • Tax Relief reimburses part of the tax for elderly or disabled owners who live in the home. For 2025 the county brochure listed up to $81 for Cleveland city residents, $99 inside the fire fringe and $101 outside it.
  • Tax Freeze was adopted by the Bradley County Commission in August 2007. The bill stays at whatever it was in the owner's first qualifying year, provided the owner remains eligible and adds no improvements.
  • Disabled veteran owners and their surviving spouses can qualify for relief paid on the first $175,000 of home market value.

All taxes must be current before relief is granted. Call the Trustee for this year's application deadline and income limit.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Cleveland property valuation?
sections.html:
Call the county Assessor of Property, (423) 728-7126, and request an informal review of the value. The appraisal staff look at your file first. If you still disagree, the next step is the Board of Equalization, which is made up of local citizens.

Appeals can be started at any time but are heard in the spring, and a decision affects only that year's tax. The county board of equalization typically sits from June 1. Filing with it keeps open your option of going to the State Board of Equalization afterward.

sections.h2: What happens if Cleveland property tax is never paid?
sections.html:
The Bradley County Clerk and Master runs the annual tax sale of delinquent parcels. Sales are open public auctions, the notice list is published two to three weeks beforehand, and the price is paid in cash, money order or check at the time of sale. The Trustee's office does not keep a mailing list.

A sale clears every lien except state and federal liens. The buyer waits a year from the filing of the sale confirmation before taking possession, and the former owner may redeem during that window. The buyer earns 10 percent a year while the redemption period runs. Call the Clerk and Master at (423) 728-7209 for the next sale.

Cleveland is the Bradley County seat and its largest city. The 2020 census counted 47,356 residents, and the July 2025 estimate is 51,172. For 2020 to 2024 there were 18,829 households and a $272,200 median owner-occupied value. Just 48.0 percent of homes are owner-occupied and median rent is $1,034, which makes a tenant in the house a real possibility.

sections.h2: Selling a Cleveland house with tax owed
sections.html:
Buyers are told to read the closing statement and ask the title company who pays. The answer depends on the transfer date, and any unpaid tax keeps building against the property meanwhile. Ask the title company to pull both county and city tax status before the contract date.

The city's online system shows whether the current tax is paid, and a duplicate bill is available from the finance office at (423) 472-4551. Partial payment agreements and payment plans with the city only work when the balance is cleared before March. A seller on one of those plans should get a payoff figure from the title company rather than assume the remaining installments transfer to the buyer.

A short sequence keeps a Cleveland closing simple:

  • Request the city balance from the finance office and the county balance from the Trustee.
  • Ask whether a payment plan is active and, if so, what it will take to close it out.
  • Have both amounts listed on the settlement statement so they are paid from the proceeds.
  • Keep the final receipts for your records.

sections.h2: What to have ready before you list
sections.html:
Gather these papers early, since a buyer's lender or the title company will ask for them.

  • Your most recent city bill and county bill, or duplicates if the originals are lost.
  • Proof that the current year is paid, or a payoff figure if it is not.
  • Any relief or freeze paperwork, because those programs require taxes to be current.
  • The Assessor's value and, if you have disputed it, the date the Board of Equalization heard the case.

With those on hand, a cash buyer or a title company can confirm the tax picture in a single call to each office, instead of waiting days on duplicate requests.

faqs.q: When is Cleveland property tax due?
faqs.a: The city bill is due starting October 1, and February 28 is the last penalty-free day. A 1.5 percent monthly charge begins in March and stops growing at 18 percent.

faqs.q: Who do I pay for property tax in Cleveland, TN?
faqs.a: Pay the City of Cleveland for the city tax and the Bradley County Trustee for the county tax. The city finance office is at 190 Church Street NE and the Trustee is at 1701 Keith Street NW.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Cleveland property tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, with limits. The city accepts partial payments if you complete forms and pay the whole amount before March 1, and it offers a twelve month plan if forms are in by February 15. Online card payments carry a 3 percent fee.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Cleveland property value?
faqs.a: Start with the county Assessor at (423) 728-7126. If you still disagree after that review, the Board of Equalization hears the appeal in spring.

faqs.q: What if I leave a Cleveland property tax bill unpaid?
faqs.a: Interest climbs by 1.5 percent each month to a cap of 18 percent, and then the debt passes to the Bradley County Clerk and Master. A parcel that stays delinquent can go to public auction, with one year to redeem.
